subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should configured cross-provider model fallback imply consent to transfer images and attachments, or should OpenClaw add a separate media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: Current code proves the media can cross provider boundaries, but the durable default affects privacy, compatibility, and fallback usefulness, so automation should not choose the trust boundary alone.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add config/docs/runtime behavior that preserves compatibility unless maintainers choose otherwise while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document full fallback consent
options.body: Keep forwarding semantics and clearly document that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text plus media.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip fallback media by default across provider boundaries and require an explicit opt-in for fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add config/docs/runtime behavior that preserves compatibility unless maintainers choose otherwise while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the active fallback media path makes this the best available owner for the immediate decision routing.
